levels.word: alternative · delay · reliable · temporary · disrupt · restore
levels.description: Six words, two kinds of practice, and one complete reading.

paragraphs.en: At the station, Lina discovers that a damaged signal will delay the last train. The station manager calls the problem temporary, but offers no reliable estimate of the departure time. Lina has an early appointment the next morning, so waiting without a plan feels risky.
paragraphs.zh: 在车站，莉娜发现信号设备损坏将使末班车延误。站长说问题只是暂时的，却没有给出可靠的发车时间。莉娜第二天一早有约，因此毫无计划地等待让她觉得不太稳妥。

paragraphs.en: A night bus is an alternative, although it stops far from her home. A taxi would cost much more. She checks the bus timetable herself instead of trusting a message from another passenger. Repairs can disrupt a journey, but poor information can make the disruption harder to manage.
paragraphs.zh: 夜班公交是另一个选择，不过下车站离她家很远。出租车则贵得多。她自己核查公交时刻表，没有轻信另一位乘客的消息。维修会打乱行程，但信息不清可能让人更难应对。

paragraphs.en: The manager eventually explains what workers are doing to restore the service. Lina chooses the bus because its arrival time is clearer, not because it is the fastest option in every situation. A useful travel plan considers uncertainty as well as distance.
paragraphs.zh: 站长终于解释了工人正如何恢复服务。莉娜选择公交，是因为到达时间更明确，而不是因为公交在所有情况下都最快。实用的出行计划既考虑路程，也考虑不确定性。

article.title: The café that ran out of bread

paragraphs.en: A small café usually sells forty sandwiches a day. When a nearby office opens, demand rises suddenly, but its bread supply stays the same. By noon, bread is scarce. Customers complain, yet buying twice as much every morning could create another problem.
paragraphs.zh: 一家小咖啡馆通常每天卖四十份三明治。附近一处办公楼启用后，需求突然增长，但面包供应量没有变化。到了中午，面包就不够了。顾客有所抱怨，不过每天早晨采购双倍面包也可能造成另一个问题。

paragraphs.en: The owner wants lunch to remain affordable. She asks customers to order before eleven and tests a smaller afternoon menu. These changes help her estimate how much food people will consume. A busy Monday does not necessarily predict a busy Friday.
paragraphs.zh: 店主希望午餐仍然价格亲民。她请顾客十一点前预订，并试行精简的下午菜单。这些改变帮助她估计大家会吃掉多少食物。忙碌的星期一不一定能预测星期五也同样忙。

paragraphs.en: At closing time, she records both missed orders and food waste. Counting only sales would hide the customers who left without buying anything. Counting only leftovers would hide the sandwiches people wanted but could not get. Good planning requires both sides of the story.
paragraphs.zh: 打烊时，她同时记录未能满足的订单和食物浪费。只统计销量会漏掉没有买到东西就离开的顾客；只统计剩饭，又会忽略人们想买却没买到的三明治。好的规划需要兼顾两方面。

paragraphs.en: A student club tests a hypothesis: a brighter lamp helps people solve puzzles faster. The first test seems promising, but one group receives easier puzzles. Because puzzle difficulty is another variable, the club cannot tell what caused the difference.
paragraphs.zh: 一个学生社团检验这样一个假设：更亮的灯能让人更快解开谜题。首次测试看起来很有希望，但其中一组拿到的题目更简单。题目难度也是一个变量，因此社团无法判断究竟是什么造成了差异。

paragraphs.en: For a fairer test, the students use puzzles of similar difficulty and assign participants by chance. They also hide the purpose of the study from the person recording times. This reduces one possible source of bias. A result that matches expectations is not automatically strong evidence.
paragraphs.zh: 为使测试更公平，学生们使用难度相近的题目，并随机分配参与者。他们还不向计时者透露研究目的，以减少一种潜在的偏差来源。结果符合预期，并不自动意味着证据很有力。

paragraphs.en: The club asks another class to replicate the test. Its results are not identical, but they are consistent in direction: the brighter lamp produces a small improvement. The students now have a better reason to continue investigating, though they still avoid claiming that every learner needs the same lamp.
paragraphs.zh: 社团请另一个班复做测试。结果并非完全相同，但方向一致：更亮的灯带来小幅改善。学生们现在有更好的理由继续研究，不过仍避免声称每位学习者都需要同一种灯。

paragraphs.en: A busy street will become a pedestrian area on weekend afternoons. One resident welcomes the quieter surroundings, while another worries about carrying groceries home. The plan sounds simple until the council asks who still needs vehicle access.
paragraphs.zh: 一条繁忙街道将在周末下午变成步行区。一位居民欢迎更安静的环境，另一位则担心如何把食品杂货搬回家。直到市政委员会开始询问谁仍需要车辆通行，这个计划才显现出复杂之处。

paragraphs.en: The council decides to restrict ordinary through traffic but allow deliveries during a short morning period. Emergency vehicles can enter at any time. The benefit of less traffic is real, yet it should not depend on pretending that everyone travels in the same way.
paragraphs.zh: 委员会决定限制一般穿行车辆，但允许早晨短时间内送货，紧急车辆则随时可以进入。交通减少确有好处，但不应以假定每个人的出行方式都相同为前提。

paragraphs.en: After a trial month, shops report more visitors and several residents report problems with loading spaces. Instead of treating either report as the whole answer, the council adjusts the timetable. Its task is to balance a shared public space with practical needs that differ from person to person.
paragraphs.zh: 试行一个月后，商铺表示访客增加，一些居民则反映装卸空间存在问题。委员会没有把任何一方的说法当作全部答案，而是调整了时间安排。它需要在共享公共空间与因人而异的实际需求之间取得平衡。

levels.word: negotiate · compromise · boundary · obligation · mutual · resolve
levels.description: Six words, two kinds of practice, and one complete reading.

paragraphs.en: Three friends share a flat and a small kitchen. At first, nobody states a boundary about borrowing food. When an expensive jar disappears, the flatmates disagree about whether sharing a home creates an obligation to share everything inside it.
paragraphs.zh: 三个朋友合租一套房，共用一个小厨房。最初，没有人明确说明借用食物的界限。一瓶昂贵的食品不见后，他们对合住是否意味着有义务共享屋内所有东西产生了分歧。

paragraphs.en: They decide to negotiate before the disagreement grows. One flatmate wants separate shelves; another wants a shelf of shared basics. Their compromise combines both ideas. Personal food needs permission, while the shared shelf is funded by a small monthly contribution.
paragraphs.zh: 他们决定趁分歧扩大前协商。一个人希望各用各的架子，另一个想设置存放共用基本食品的架子。最终的折中方案结合了两种想法：使用私人食品须先获准，共用架子则由每月少量共同出资维持。

paragraphs.en: The agreement cannot resolve every future problem, so they arrange a short monthly conversation. Mutual respect is easier to maintain when expectations are visible. Being friendly does not require guessing what another person is willing to give.
paragraphs.zh: 协议不能解决未来所有问题，因此他们约好每月简短沟通一次。把彼此的期望说清楚，更有利于维持相互尊重。友好相处不应该要求人们猜测别人愿意付出什么。

article.title: One more year for a jacket

paragraphs.en: Nora almost throws away a jacket with a torn pocket. Its outer fabric is durable, but the thin lining is fragile. A repairer explains that one weak part does not mean the whole garment has reached the end of its useful life.
paragraphs.zh: 诺拉差点扔掉一件口袋破损的夹克。外层布料耐用，但薄内衬比较脆弱。修衣师解释说，一个部位不结实，并不意味着整件衣服都已经不能再用。

paragraphs.en: They choose to replace the pocket lining and retain the original buttons. Nora also learns how to maintain the fabric between repairs. A repair that lasts requires attention to structure, not merely a patch that looks tidy for a day.
paragraphs.zh: 他们决定更换口袋内衬，保留原来的纽扣。诺拉还学会了在两次维修之间如何保养布料。持久的修补需要关注结构，而不只是贴一块能整洁一天的补丁。

paragraphs.en: The repairer can adapt the pocket opening so Nora can reach it more easily. This small change makes the jacket more useful to its owner. Keeping an object does not always mean keeping every detail unchanged; thoughtful alteration can help it stay in use.
paragraphs.zh: 修衣师可以调整口袋开口，让诺拉取物更方便。这个小改动让夹克更适合主人使用。保留一件物品，不一定意味着每个细节都必须原封不动；经过思考的修改能帮助它继续发挥作用。

levels.title: Two labels for one painting
levels.word: interpret · context · perspective · ambiguous · contrast · subtle
levels.description: Six words, two kinds of practice, and one complete reading.

paragraphs.en: In a small museum, visitors are asked to interpret the same painting before and after reading a label. Without context, one visitor sees a cheerful family scene. After learning that the artist painted it during a separation, the visitor notices the empty chair differently.
paragraphs.zh: 在一家小博物馆，访客被请去在阅读说明牌前后解读同一幅画。没有背景信息时，一位访客看到的是欢乐的家庭场景；知道画家在与家人分离期间创作此画后，他对空椅子的感受发生了变化。

paragraphs.en: The museum does not announce that the first perspective was foolish. The expression on one face is ambiguous, and a subtle shadow can suggest more than one mood. A label may guide attention without settling every question about what an image means.
paragraphs.zh: 博物馆没有宣称第一种视角愚蠢。画中一张脸的表情并不明确，一处细微阴影也可能让人感受到不止一种情绪。说明牌可以引导注意，却不能决定图像含义的所有问题。

paragraphs.en: To make the contrast clearer, the curator places two short descriptions side by side. One discusses color; the other discusses the artist’s letters. Visitors compare what each description helps them notice. The exercise rewards careful looking rather than a race to guess the museum’s favorite answer.
paragraphs.zh: 为使对比更清楚，策展人并排放置两段简短说明，一段谈色彩，另一段谈画家的书信。访客比较每段说明分别帮助他们注意到什么。这项活动鼓励细致观察，而不是争先猜出博物馆偏好的答案。

readingQuestions.prompt: How does the label change the visitor’s experience?
readingQuestions.translation: 说明牌如何改变了访客的体验？
options: It forces the visitor to ignore the empty chair.
It offers background that changes what the visitor notices.
It proves that color has no role in the painting.
readingQuestions.answer: It offers background that changes what the visitor notices.
readingQuestions.explanation: Knowing about the separation gives the empty chair a new significance.
readingQuestions.explanationZh: 得知分离的背景后，空椅子具有了新的意义。

readingQuestions.prompt: What is the main purpose of the two descriptions?
readingQuestions.translation: 两段说明的主要目的是什么？
options: To show how different information can guide attention.
To identify which visitor is the fastest reader.
To remove every possible ambiguity from the painting.
readingQuestions.answer: To show how different information can guide attention.
readingQuestions.explanation: Visitors compare the insights made possible by the color description and the letters.
readingQuestions.explanationZh: 访客比较色彩说明与书信信息分别带来的理解。
